entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the revisionists that husband of opposite party no. 2 is mentally unfit.

The revisionists are brothers-in-law of opposite party no. 2 and they have been falsely implicated by opposite party no. 2 making false and concocted allegations in order to settle her personal score.
The revisionists have not committed any wrong with opposite party no. 2 to constitute any offence as alleged by her.
The discharge application of the revisionists has been illegally rejected by learned Magistrate.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. representing the State and learned counsel for opposite party no.
2 reiterating the prosecution case as mentioned in the first information report dated 08.08.2019 submit that since husband of opposite party no. 2 is mentally sick, therefore, the revisionists, who are brothers-in-law of opposite party no. 2, taking benefit of this situation started harassing and torturing opposite party no. 2 in her matrimonial home.
They have also extorted money from father of opposite party no. 2 and thereafter she was thrown out from her matrimonial home.
It is also pointed out that on 16.02.2024, charges have also been framed against the revisionists.
Having heard submission of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, I find that it is not in dispute that charges have been framed on 16.02.2024 against the revisionists.
The trial has started and statement of PW-1 is going on.

The Apex Court in the case of Ratilal Bhanji Mithani Vs.
State of Maharashtra and others, (1979) 2 SCC 179 has held that after framing of charge, the question of discharge does not arise.

entities.text:
Ratilal Bhanji Mithani Vs.
State of Maharashtra and others, (1979) 2 SCC 179
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said view has been reiterated by the Apex Court in the case of Stree Atyachar Virodhi Parishad Vs. Dilip Nathumal Chordia and another, (1989) 1 SCC 715.

entities.text: Stree Atyachar Virodhi Parishad Vs. Dilip Nathumal Chordia and another, (1989) 1 SCC 715
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the stage of trial as noted above, this Court is also of the view that once the charges are framed, accused is put to trial and thereafter the accused may either be acquitted or convicted but he cannot be discharged.
The discharge post framing of charge is not recognized in the Criminal Procedure Code.
It is also well settled that even when there are materials raising strong suspicion against the accused, the Court will be justified in rejecting the prayer for discharge.
In view of the above, I do not find any good ground to interfere in the impugned order dated 25.04.2023.
The criminal revision lacks merit and is accordingly, dismissed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Apex Court in the case of Ratilal Bhanji Mithani Vs.
State of Maharashtra and others, (1979) 2 SCC 179 has held that after framing of charge, the question of discharge does not arise.
The said view has been reiterated by the Apex Court in the case of Stree Atyachar Virodhi Parishad Vs. Dilip Nathumal Chordia and another, (1989) 1 SCC 715.
Considering the stage of trial as noted above, this Court is also of the view that once the charges are framed, accused is put to trial and thereafter the accused may either be acquitted or convicted but he cannot be discharged.
The discharge post framing of charge is not recognized in the Criminal Procedure Code.
It is also well settled that even when there are materials raising strong suspicion against the accused, the Court will be justified in rejecting the prayer for discharge.

The criminal revision lacks merit and is accordingly, dismissed.
